full_judgment: 5. Thereupon the defendant moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. At the time of hearing of the Rule it was urged that the plaintiff being a party to the document in question the suit so filed seeking declaration was not maintainable as plaintiff was required to file suit in the light of the provision of section 39 of the Specific Relief Act, that the suit so filed was barred by limitation since the same was filed on February 4, 1986 though the deed of exchange was execute on December 24, 1980, that the suit was filed without seeking consequential relief of recovery of khas possession, as such was not maintainable. It may be mentioned the Court of facts i.e. the trial Court as well as the appellate Court have concurrently held that the plaintiff is in possession of the `Ka' schedule land. The High Court Division has observed that the defendant failed to show that he delivered possession of the 'Kha' schedule land to the plaintiff and that defendant also failed to produce any paper in support of his title in the `Kha' schedule land. The High Court Division discharged the Rule upon observing that the courts below concurrently held that defendant practiced fraud on the plaintiff with the view to grab the 'Ka' schedule land and the courts below also found that the plaintiff is in possession of the 'Ka' schedule land. The High Court Division further observed that defendant-petitioner miserably failed to show that the findings so arrived at by the appellate Court as well as by the trial Court are not supported by the evidence on record or that the same have been made on misreading or non-consideration of the evidence. On the question of limitation the High Court Division has observed that since the suit is very much maintainable as framed in the light of the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that as it has been found by the courts below the plaintiff is in possession of the 'Ka' schedule land as such the suit is not barred by limitation. The High Court Division as regard the other contention that the suit ought to have been filed in the light of the provision of section 39 of the Specific Relief Act has held that since there has been allegation of fraud against the defendant and the same has been established, the suit so filed seeking declaration is very much maintainable in the light of the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the plaintiff was not required to file the suit as contended by the defendant in the light of the provision of section 39 of the Specific Relief Act.
